messages:
Jules (IC): hey team — about to adopt and will be starting leave in Sept. can i change my FSA/HSA and 401k elections now or is it too late mid-plan year? quick QOL event.

Marta (People Ops): congrats! :tada: adoption counts as a qualifying life event (QLE). you can submit midyear election changes for healthcare FSAs and 401k within 60 days of the event. HSA changes depend on payroll enrollment status.

Eli (Payroll): process: for 401k we need the updated election in the portal by the next payroll cutoff to start withholding. for FSA election changes we need the completed FSA QLE form + supporting doc (placement/adoption paperwork) within 60 days. portal link: https://hr.redwood.com/benefits/qle

Jules (IC): ok timeline: baby placement is 2026-08-10. if i upload docs on 8/15 is that fine?

Sam (Benefits): yes 8/15 is within 60 days. we'll approve the FSA change and adjust deductions prospectively. note: FSAs usually cannot receive retroactive deposits for prior paychecks.

Eli (Payroll): clarifying 401k: we can increase or change % going forward. we cannot collect missed deferrals from earlier paychecks. if you want to front-load more before leave, submit a change before the cutoff. next cutoff for 8/29 pay is 2026-08-20.

Jules (IC): what about HSA pre-tax payroll contributions — can i pause them and resume at different levels?

Sam (Benefits): HSA: you can change payroll HSA deductions with a QLE if your coverage changes. if you pause during unpaid leave you can contribute directly to HSA after-tax and claim deduction on your return. employer HSA contributions follow payroll (usually stop if you have no payroll deferrals).

Eli (Payroll): a couple of extra notes: - if you elect to continue health coverage during unpaid leave, you may need to switch to COBRA or continuation; that can affect your pre-tax elections. - manager approval is not required for these election changes, only for leave itself.

Jules (IC): will employer match for 401k continue if i'm on unpaid leave?

Sam (Benefits): match is tied to payroll contributions. if there are no employee deferrals, there's nothing to match. we can escalate to leadership for a discretionary contribution in special cases but it's not standard.

Marta (People Ops): action items: Jules, 1) submit FSA QLE form + placement docs by 2026-10-09 max, 2) update 401k election in portal by 2026-08-20 if you want the higher deferral before leave, 3) DM payroll if you want help front-loading. i'll add this QLE workflow to the handbook.

Benefits Bot: QLE packet (qle_202608) emailed to Jules. :email:

Jules (IC): perfect, thanks all. i'll upload docs today and aim for the 8/20 cutoff for the payroll bump.
